notes: GR1 fixes what a SIGN clause does on a numeric entry whose PICTURE has S. Both agents' probes (scaled, edited-source and sum-counter cases) and mine print the separate leading or trailing sign correctly, and SIGN on a group or on a non-S PICTURE is refused. The refuter's c6 case, a level-01 elementary report group entry carrying PICTURE/SIGN/COLUMN/SOURCE, is accepted at 85 and prints '-03'. That entry violates the report-group-entry format: the first entry must be format 1, which has no PICTURE, SIGN, COLUMN or SOURCE, and format 3's level is 02 to 49. That under-rejection belongs to the format rule (1985-SR-XIII.3.9.3-3 / -4), not to the SIGN rule, whose effect on the entry is correct. Filed below as a lead for that rule. ATTACK SURFACE: a reader who takes 'numeric data description entry' in SR1 to include the entry's legality would make this row PARTIAL.

next.reason: 1985 report-writer SIGN: 'The SIGN clause applies only to numeric data description entries whose PICTURE contains the character S' (with §1985:XIII.3.17.3 SR1), so a group report entry may not carry it. 2023 §2023:13.18.52.4 GR1 adds 'or for each numeric item subordinate to the group to which it applies'; §2023:13.18.52.3 SR1 allows 'an alphanumeric group item, national group item, or strongly-typed group item', and §2023:13.15.3 SR11 does not confine SIGN to elementary report entries. A report group entry with SIGN over numeric 'S' items, refused by 1985, is accepted: a case added. Kept: position and mode of the sign, and §2023:13.18.52.4 GR4 / §2023:13.18.40.4 GR14 'S' 'indicates the presence, but neither the representation nor, necessarily, the position of an operational sign'.
